o1.biggest_strength: The strategic grasp of SaaS economics is exceptional—it properly treats free Podia accounts as zero-marginal-cost perks to preserve the $40k cash budget for content and activation, while matching the rival's 40% first-year hook on top partners with rigorous cost modeling.
o1.biggest_mistake: Adding both the 40% partner year-one commission bump and a 90-day window increases total payout liability, which will need very firm finance sign-off.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: It is already a 10—practically pitch-perfect for a SaaS founder.

o2.biggest_strength: Crystal-clear breakdown of the break-even risk on the 20% cut and the practical explanation of why dropping the payout threshold to $25 unlocks monthly payouts for small referrers.
o2.biggest_mistake: Allocating $12,480 of our scarce $40,000 partner perk cash budget to free Podia software subscriptions that cost the business virtually nothing to provision.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Reallocate the $12.5k wasted on list-price software licenses into real creator incentives or co-marketing, and give a clearer reason for keeping a single commission tier despite the 40% rival threat.

reason: Both nailed the core numbers and rightly killed the 20% cut, but Output 1 understands software marketing far better: it gives away Podia accounts at zero cost rather than burning $12.5k of real marketing cash on our own software, and its activation bonus and tier design directly solve our competitive threats.
